preamble: No verified case of a direct /s/ > /tʲ/ sound change has been found. The previously cited Old Irish rule (/s/ > /tʲ/ before /i/ or /e/) does not exist in the standard descriptions of Old Irish phonology, where /s/ before front vowels is simply palatalized to /sʲ/ (later Irish [ʃ]). The reverse direction, /tʲ/ > /s/ or /tʲ/ > /ʃ/ via assibilation, is the cross-linguistically common change.

examples.note: Palatalization of /s/ in Old Irish yields palatalized /sʲ/, not a stop /tʲ/; no Old Irish /s/ > /tʲ/ rule is attested

sources: Thurneysen, R. (1946). A Grammar of Old Irish. Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies.
